REQUEST for Proposals

Website Management, Content Development, and Electronic Newsletter Services

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ text_font=”||||||||” text_font_size=”17px” text_line_height=”1.8em” background_size=”initial” background_position=”top_left” background_repeat=”repeat” min_height=”475.9px” custom_padding=”||0px|||” global_colors_info=”{}”]

The Workforce Connection, Inc. (TWC) is soliciting proposals from qualified firms to
provide comprehensive website management, website content development, social media
posting and monitoring, and bi-monthly electronic newsletter services. The selected
contractor will support TWC’s digital communications by maintaining a secure,
accessible, and engaging online presence while assisting with public outreach and
stakeholder communications.

Specifications for submitting a proposal and RFP timeline are available within the Request for Proposals document and attachments, available to view and/or download below.

All questions, other than those raised at any Pre-Response conference, that pertain to this Solicitation must be submitted in written form directly to the Solicitation Contact no later than September 30, 2026. Questions received and Agency responses may be posted to the Published Procurement Information specified in Section B.1 at https://theworkforceconnection.org/request-for-proposals-bids/; only these written answers to questions shall be binding. Respondents are responsible for monitoring the site for updates.

Solicitation Contact: Joan Rabe
Agency: The Workforce Connection
Address: 303 North Main Street, Rockford, Illinois 61101
Email:  jrabe@theworkforceconnection.org

Due to the large volume of questions, the deadline for proposals has been extended from October 2 to October 9, 5p.m. CST.


Click below to view and/or download the Request for Proposals, Attachments, and FAQ’s.

title.rendered: A Foundation For The Future: Teba’s Internship Journey

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” custom_padding=”||54px|||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” text_font_size=”22px” custom_padding=”||2px|0px||” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″]

We had the pleasure of meeting Teba (pictured above on the left with Michelle Cassaro of the Chicago Rockford International Airport on the right), who shared her thoughts on her internship experience at the Chicago Rockford International Airport. She was kind enough to share her speech with us, which is below.

“My experience here at the Chicago Rockford International Airport has truly been exceptional. I’ve been given the opportunity to develop essential skills that I know will stay with me as I move forward in my future career.

The staff at RFD are some of the most genuine and hardworking people I’ve ever had the pleasure of working with. They are sincere, kind, and incredibly supportive, the list could go on. I was even offered the opportunity to become an official airport intern for the summer, something I never would have expected, but am incredibly grateful for. Over time, I’ve grown close to everyone here, and when this internship comes to an end, I know it will be difficult to say goodbye. The staff have always been willing to lend a helping hand without hesitation. For example, Shelly is always willing to invite me into her office and show me the projects she works on, guiding me through the processes and providing me with an insight into her day-to-day work life. She invites me to meetings, feeds me, and challenges me to grow, all while making sure that I enjoy the experience. What stood out the most to me is that I was never made to feel like an outsider—even as the youngest and only intern in the administrative building. I will always be grateful for the time, effort, and care everyone put into helping me learn and expand my knowledge in the business field.

While on the topic of business, it is something I want to pursue seriously. I aspire to one day become an entrepreneur, working alongside my dad as a team. My time in Human Resources at RFD has helped me develop valuable skills in leadership, organization, and decision-making. One of my favorite experiences has been participating in interviewing candidates for job openings and taking care of the application and hiring processes. It’s been exciting to meet a wide variety of people and apply my judgment and communication abilities in a real-world setting. I’ve discovered that I really enjoy this aspect of business, and it’s an area where I feel I’ve grown the most. This experience will directly support my future goals, as I know I’ll need these same skills when building and managing my own business.

I would like to take a moment to recognize and thank my family, who are here supporting me from the stands today. Your presence means more to me than words can fully express. From the very beginning, you have poured your time, love, and wisdom into raising me, always guiding me with care and teaching me the values that have shaped who I am. You gave me the strength to face challenges, the encouragement to keep going when things felt difficult, and the belief that I could achieve more than I ever imagined. Because of you, I stand here today as a strong, driven, and determined young woman. Everything I have accomplished is rooted in the foundation you built for me, and I carry your lessons with me in everything I do. I am endlessly grateful for your sacrifices, your patience, and your unwavering support, and I hope to continue making you proud in all that lies ahead.

In closing, I want to, again, express my gratitude to all the RFD staff for everything you’ve done for me. I also owe a tremendous thank you to Berenice and the Workforce Connection. Without your offer and support, I wouldn’t have had the opportunity to develop these new skills, gain valuable experience, and work alongside such incredible people over the past few months. From the bottom of my heart, thank you all. I will never forget the impact you’ve had on my journey or the opportunities you’ve given me.”

Click here to learn about the employer’s perspective on their experience hosting Teba as an intern. 

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

title.rendered: The Power of Opportunity: Zaria Shared Her Story

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” custom_padding=”||54px|||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” text_font_size=”22px” custom_padding=”||2px|0px||” global_colors_info=”{}”]

We were honored to have Zaria speak at our Board meeting about her journey with The Workforce Connection, Awaken Foundation and Goodwill Industries of Northern Illinois, all who provided opportunities for her to learn, grow and succeed. We are very proud of Zaria for her hard work and dedication.

Zaria graciously provided her speech for us so that we could share that with you.

“My name is Zaria, and I am a proud 2025 graduate of the Awaken Foundation Program.

I began my journey during a difficult time in my life. I felt lost, unsure of my direction and disconnected from opportunities until I learned about Awaken Program through someone in my community. I saw an opportunity to make a positive change in my life. My goal was to get back on the right path and build a meaningful career.

Through the program, I developed valuable workplace skills, including communication, teamwork, professionalism, and employability. I also learned the importance of showing up every day prepared, committed, and ready to grow. Most importantly, the program gave me exposure to career opportunities I had never considered before.

One of those opportunities led me to Goodwill Industries of Northern Illinois, where I began as a WEX (work experience/internship) and now serve as an Administrative and Program Coordinator. In this role, I have gained invaluable experience and learned so much from the incredible leaders, mentors, and coworkers who have supported my growth. I am grateful to be part of such a dedicated team.

Today, I stand before you as an example of what can happen when workforce development programs provide individuals with training, support, and real opportunities. These programs do more than prepare people for employment—they help transform lives.

I would like to thank the Workforce Board, the Awaken Foundation, the instructors, staff, Goodwill Industries of Northern Illinois, and all of the community partners who invest in programs like this. Your commitment creates opportunities for people to build brighter futures and achieve goals they may have once thought were out of reach.

My life is moving in a very different direction today than it was when I first walked through the doors of this program. I am proud of how far I have come, and I am excited about where I am headed. For that, I am deeply thankful.

Thank you for believing in the potential of others and for recognizing that people do deserve second chances, opportunities to grow, succeed, and build a better future.”

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

title.rendered: Setting the Foundation for Success: Jada’s Internship Journey

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” custom_padding=”||54px|||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” text_font_size=”22px” custom_padding=”||2px|0px||” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″]

Through the Elevate Youth Program at The Workforce Connection, Jada was able to complete a Work Experience Internship at Athletico Physical Therapy, where she aspires to become a physical therapist. Jada will be attending Marquette University in the fall and is very appreciative of the opportunity this internship has provided through the Elevate Program. Jada shared the following thoughts about her overall experience:

Jada shared “My experience with the Elevate Program and at Athletico Physical Therapy has been nothing short of amazing. Having the opportunity to be a part of the internship program has made me 100 percent sure that I want to pursue a career in physical therapy. The people that I have worked with have really made this experience worthwhile. I have learned so much from everyone and they treat me like someone who has been part of the team for a long time. The environment is very welcoming and full of laughter and fun. The patients I get to interact with have also been truly amazing and friendly. I have learned that all parts of my internship is important from cleaning equipment and folding towels, to being able to do things a real physical therapy aide would do, such as take calls, set up a patient’s exercises, and even help the patients with some of the exercises. I am truly blessed and grateful for this opportunity and I know I am set up for success in the future!”

The Workforce Connection and Elevate is very proud of Jada and look forward to all of her future endeavors. 

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

Rylee is a dedicated participant in The Workforce Connection’s Elevate Program and recently completed her internship with North Boone Fire District No. 3. A senior at Harlem High School, Rylee is on track to graduate this year and is already taking meaningful steps toward her future career goals.

Rylee aspires to become an EMT and ultimately a firefighter. During her internship, she successfully completed several training courses through the North Boone Fire District, keeping her on track to meet certification requirements. Her supervisor has expressed how impressed he is with her strong commitment, leadership potential, and determination to give her best in everything she does.

Through the Elevate Program, Rylee was able to participate in a paid internship and receive transportation support services that have been invaluable while balancing her responsibilities as a high school student. Rylee demonstrates a deep commitment to her community by helping those in need. She continues to work hard and proudly represents the North Boone Fire District at community resource events, serving as a team leader and a positive example of a young person pursuing a career in emergency services.

We are incredibly proud of Rylee and her success in the Elevate Program!

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ theme_builder_area=”post_content” _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” min_height=”1010.9px”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” column_structure=”1_2,1_2″ theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” type=”1_2″ theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_blurb title=”Karen Brown” image=”https://theworkforceconnection.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Karen-Brown-e1778180870681.jpg” _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” theme_builder_area=”post_content” header_font=”|700|||||||” header_text_color=”#0C71C3″ hover_enabled=”0″ sticky_enabled=”0″ alt=”Headshot of smiling woman with light brown hair, brown eyes, black suit jacket and pearl necklace.” title_text=”Karen Brown”]

The Workforce Connection Board extends its sincere appreciation to Karen Brown on her retirement from Highland Community College and, consequently, from the Board. Karen has been a dedicated and integral member of the Board since 2000. Over more than two decades of service, she has provided thoughtful leadership and steadfast commitment in numerous roles, including Board Chair, Immediate Past Chair, Secretary/Treasurer, and Chair of both the Finance and Human Resources Committees.

Reflecting on her time on the Board, Karen shared: “When I first joined, it was the Workforce Investment Board, which then became the Northern Illinois Workforce Alliance and, now today, it is The Workforce Connection Board. While it has gone through a few name and location changes, the mission has stayed constant. During my time spent on the Board, I have always appreciated the valuable work we do to develop our workforce and positively impact the lives of many individuals and businesses in our community.”

Although retiring, Karen will continue to be involved in the Rockford area business community through human resources and leadership consulting with FurstConsulting and by teaching human resources courses.

[/et_pb_blurb][/et_pb_column][et_pb_column _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” type=”1_2″ theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_blurb title=”Len Carter” image=”https://theworkforceconnection.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Len-Carter-Headshot-edited-3.png” _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” theme_builder_area=”post_content” header_font=”|700|||||||” header_text_color=”#0C71C3″ hover_enabled=”0″ sticky_enabled=”0″ alt=”Headshot of smiling brown haired man with a tan suit, colorful tie, and glasses.” title_text=”Len Carter Headshot edited 3″]

After a long and distinguished career, Len Carter has retired from FHN. With his retirement, Len has also concluded his service on The Workforce Connection Board, where he has been a dedicated and influential member for nearly two decades. Len served as Board Chair starting in 2007 and later as a Director on the Board.

When asked about his time on the Board, Len shared: “It has been an honor and privilege to serve on this Board and to witness the meaningful impact it has had across our region. My tenure goes way back to my service as a member–and later Chair–of the Northwest Region WIB Board. The individuals on this Board and the staff will always hold a special place in my heart. There is still much work to be done–don’t take the foot off the pedal!”

In retirement, Len plans to remain active through projects, teaching, and speaking engagements.

[/et_pb_blurb][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ theme_builder_area=”post_content” _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” type=”4_4″ theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” theme_builder_area=”post_content” hover_enabled=”0″ sticky_enabled=”0″]

The Workforce Connection (TWC) was proud to present at the National Association of Workforce Boards (NAWB) Forum in late March.

 The session, titled “Leveraging Industry Partnerships to Tool Up Tomorrow’s Workforce,” highlighted how apprenticeships—along with partnerships between workforce boards and businesses—can address immediate hiring needs while preparing for long-term workforce sustainability. Attendees learned how one business created a favorable environment for in-house training as well as how a workforce board can support business partners in establishing apprenticeships.

The session featured a strong lineup of local leadership including:

  • Dr. Gina Caronna, TWC President & CEO,
  • Shelly Cassaro, TWC Board Chair/Deputy Director of Finance and Administration-Chicago Rockford International Airport
  • Todd Wells, TWC Board Vice Chair/Vice President of Operations-Bourn & Koch

 Together, they shared real-world strategies and innovative approaches happening right here in our region.

Public Comment Period Closed


The Workforce Connection, Inc.
Local Workforce Innovation Area 3 (LWIA3)
2026 Modification to the 2024-2028 Regional and Local Plan

Under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA), Local Workforce Innovation Area (LWIA) Regional and Local Plans are comprehensive four-year strategies developed to align workforce development, education and economic development activities, with the current cycle running from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2028, with a required two-year review in 2026.

The Workforce Connection, Inc. (TWC) Regional and Local Plan consists of regional and local plan components.  The plan was developed through a robust collaboration with business, economic development, education and workforce development stakeholders, and will align efforts across the Northern Stateline Economic Development Region which includes Boone, Winnebago, Stephenson and Ogle counties.  In addition to the regional plan component, TWC developed a four-year local action plan to direct strategies and investments in Boone, Stephenson and Winnebago counties, which makes up its local workforce area. 

The Draft 2026 Modification to the 2024-2028 Regional and Local Plan is available for public comment through March 13, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. CST. Public comment period is now closed.

Click below to view or download the draft modified plan and to submit your comments.

Upon approval by the State of Illinois, the modified plan would be effective July 1, 2026.

title.rendered: Earning and Learning: Cosmetology Training that Pays

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” custom_padding=”||54px|||” global_colors_info=”{}” custom_margin=”||-64px|||” min_height=”1236.4px”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” text_font_size=”22px” custom_padding=”||2px|0px||” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Style House Seven, a woman-owned salon in Rockford, is transforming how individuals begin their careers in cosmetology. Their apprenticeship program uses a structured, progressive wage model that allows apprentices to steadily increase their earnings as they develop new skills, all while feeling supported both personally and professionally.

The Workforce Connection’s Apprenticeship Specialist, Collin Ruthe, collaborated with Style House Seven to navigate the information-gathering process and complete the registration of the apprenticeship program with the Department of Labor—demonstrating how strategic partnerships like this are advancing workforce development by expanding access to high-quality apprenticeship opportunities.

What sets this program apart is the comprehensive training curriculum personally designed by owner Lorleanne Ball (pictured above)— a stylist, mentor, and community advocate who has seen firsthand the real demands of the beauty industry. Traditionally, stylists must pay out of pocket for advanced training to grow their skills and income potential. At Style House Seven, apprentices receive that same high-value education while being paid, removing financial barriers and opening more doors to long-term career success.

Cosmetology pathways often require students to finance costly schooling and ongoing skill development. To meet that challenge with experience, Style House Seven created its own internal training curriculum and launched a paid apprenticeship program in December 2025 and now is supported by our workforce apprenticeship grant. The Co-Stylist Program provides a structured, hands-on pathway where apprentices assist lead stylists, participate in weekly training sessions, and practice services in a supervised environment. With wages subsidized through The Workforce Connection, apprentices can focus on learning — not worrying about how to afford additional education.

A second co-stylist apprentice has recently begun training under this curriculum, made possible through support from The Workforce Connection. Their early progress already shows that this model works: apprentices are gaining confidence, mastering foundational skills, and becoming valued members of the team. This approach benefits everyone — apprentices earn while they learn, the salon builds a strong talent pipeline through mentorship, and the community gains expanded apprenticeship opportunities beyond traditional trades.

At the heart of Style House Seven’s success is a belief in people — not just employees, but neighbors, clients, and local partners. Investing in a team is also investing in the community that makes a business shine. By supporting small businesses that think creatively about workforce development, we help broaden career pathways and ensure more occupations offer sustainable, long-term opportunities right here in Rockford.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

Hear from our partipant, Elaine, who achieved her nursing career goals with the help of The Workforce Connection’s program…

“Having The Workforce Connection help me get through school has been one of my biggest blessings. What being a nurse means to me is helping people on their hardest days. Even when there are difficulties in my life, knowing that I can help my patients and put a smile on their faces means the world to me.

Being able to complete this program and becoming a nurse means that I am to provide for myself while my family can’t. Once again I am forever grateful for my case worker Jackie and this organization for helping me make my dreams come true. “ Elaine

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

Chris enrolled in The Workforce Connection’s youth program Elevate in February 2025. Since then, he earned his GED through GoodGrads and attended the CEJA program. His goal is to become a Computer Information Systems Specialist. Chris used TWC funding to attend IT classes at Rock Valley College while completing his Work Experience in Goodwill’s IT Department, gaining hands-on IT practice. He contributed to the IT team setting up the Excel Center and worked on the Customer Support Team. Chris consistently received positive feedback from his supervisor, management, and peers.

Chris shares that all the programs he participated in through TWC’s Elevate Program and Goodwill have been his most positive experience so far. The encouragement, kindness, and support have been wonderful.

Chris, we are so proud of you and confident you will achieve everything you pursue.

 

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

Derek participated in The Workforce Connection’s Elevate Program and is a recent graduate of Harlem High School. He aspires to become an Advanced Auto Technician and completed his work experience at Tuffy Auto Repair.

During the 14 weeks of the paid internship, he gained experience in performing standard maintenance on both foreign and domestic vehicles.

Derek’s supervisor, Jim Heim, commented on his ambition, dependability, and quick learning ability, stating that he was a great team member. Derek expressed his gratefulness for The Workforce Connection.

Leandra joined The Workforce Connection’s Elevate Youth program to pursue her Certified Nursing Assistant license and completed her training through the Castor Health Institute in Freeport, IL. With the support and guidance of her instructors and TWC staff, she successfully passed her Illinois Nurse Assistant Competency Exam (INACE) exam.

Leandra is grateful for the experience and for the Elevate Program, which provided valuable resources such as tuition assistance and a gas card to get to and from class. Today, she is a proud licensed CNA, working full-time with Castor Health Solutions!

This fall, an innovative partnership came full circle. On September 30th, three apprentices graduated from a new industrial sewing apprenticeship, officially sponsored by Tad More Tailoring, the first registered program of its kind in the area. The Workforce Connection proudly played a key role in coordinating and submitting the apprenticeship for registration with the U.S. Department of Labor, helping bring Tad More’s vision for training and sustainability to life.

The program offers a well-rounded experience, blending technical sewing skills with entry-level workplace training to prepare participants for long-term success. Tad More’s focus on reducing waste and maximizing resources gives the program a unique edge, combining job readiness with a commitment to sustainable manufacturing practices.

We are proud to have supported this collaborative effort and even prouder to see the first cohort cross the finish line.

The graduates are pictured above and below, along with Sarene Alsharif of Tad More Tailoring and Alterations (below right).

Strategic Partnership Advances Apprenticeship Success

Rockford Toolcraft Inc. continues to lead in workforce development through its active participation in the RRVTMA Apprenticeship Program. As part of its broader commitment to expanding talent pipelines in manufacturing, Rockford Toolcraft partnered with The Workforce Connection (TWC) to provide tuition reimbursements for classroom instruction delivered through Rock Valley College.

This collaboration reflects Rockford Toolcraft’s ongoing commitment to developing skilled talent through a combination of hands-on training and classroom instruction. By combining structured learning with real-world experience, the program equips apprentices with the knowledge and confidence they need to succeed and grow within the industry.

Lukas Bell (pictured above), an apprentice at Rockford Toolcraft, is making remarkable progress in his Tool & Die Maker Apprenticeship through RRVTMA. “Being in the apprenticeship program has helped me build confidence and technical skills on the job,” he said. “It’s a great opportunity to grow while working full time.”

These types of partnerships between The Workforce Connection, employers, and educators support a strong regional talent pipeline, while keeping leadership and direction where it belongs: with the employers shaping the future of manufacturing.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

title.rendered: Rite-Way and Kristopher’s On-the-Job Training Success Story

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ theme_builder_area=”post_content” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” column_structure=”1_2,1_2″ theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” type=”1_2″ theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_blurb title=”Kristopher’s Success through the On-the-Job Training Program” image=”https://theworkforceconnection.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Kristopher-Wall-Photo-web-edit-scaled.jpg” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” theme_builder_area=”post_content” hover_enabled=”0″ sticky_enabled=”0″ alt=”Photo of job training, Kristopher, wearing a red shirt and jeans and standing in a furniture store.” title_text=”Kristopher Wall Photo web edit” image_icon_width=”94%” header_font=”|700|||||||” header_font_size=”23px” header_text_color=”#0c71c3″ body_font_size=”20px”]

 

Kristopher (pictured above) was looking for a change of employment and Rite-Way Furniture was just the place to help him succeed! TWC assisted Kris with his training and gave him career guidance. Kris is now the Assistant Manager at Rite-Way furniture, and he has a bright future ahead of him!

 

[/et_pb_blurb][/et_pb_column][et_pb_column _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” type=”1_2″ theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_blurb title=”Rite-Way On-the-Job Training Partnership” image=”https://theworkforceconnection.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Cal-Rite-Way-web-edit-scaled.jpeg” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” theme_builder_area=”post_content” hover_enabled=”0″ sticky_enabled=”0″ alt=”Photo introduces a part of the story about Rite-Way and features a man who is standing and wearing dark dress pants, a dress shirt, and tie. The man is standing in front of furniture displays including couches and chairs.” title_text=”Cal Rite-Way web edit” header_font=”|700|||||||” header_text_color=”#0c71c3″ header_font_size=”23px” body_font_size=”20px” image_icon_width=”120%”]

 

Rite-Way Furniture was looking for talent and reached out to The Workforce Connection (TWC) for help with their staffing needs. Cal Wescott (pictured to the right), owner of Rite-Way, knew of a candidate looking for a new career path and TWC’s Business Services Team worked with Cal to form an On-the-Job Training partnership.

This innovative partnership in which TWC provided funding to help offset the costs of training a new employee and Rite-Way provided mentorship and hands-on experience…the results have been a win-win! The partnership is a testament to the power of opportunity, guidance, and community.

The Workforce Connection and Rite-Way’s commitment to growing talent from within the community is a testament of the power of opportunity, guidance, and community.

[/et_pb_blurb][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

With WIOA funding from The Workforce Connection (TWC), Ruthie is currently pursuing an Associate of Applied Science (AAS) degree in Aviation Maintenance Technology at Rock Valley College (RVC). TWC has also been able to provide Ruthie with transportation assistance in the form of gas cards to get to and from class. In addition, through our JTED grant, we’ve been able to help Ruthie purchase her required tools and books for her AAS program at RVC.

We wanted to share that Ruthie was already a licensed civilian pilot by the age of 17, and was recently featured in a WIFR news video about earning her wings as a certified Civil Air Patrol (CAP) Pilot with the Rockford Composite Squadron.

All of us at TWC are inspired by Ruthie’s amazing determination and hard work. Click here to view the WIFR news video.

Photo Credit: Thumbnail photo of Ruthie above is a snapshot from the WIFR video to introduce this story..

After gaining hands-on experience in the automotive industry as both a Counter Associate and Detailer, Daniel was eager to expand his skill set and take on greater responsibilities in a new setting. With support from The Workforce Connection, he was introduced to Barkau CDJR, where an opportunity as a Parts Manager was available. Daniel was partnered with Barkau’s Service Director, who provided mentorship in essential areas such as automotive inventory management and related operational skills.

Today, Daniel takes great pride in how this role has launched him into a promising new career path. He remains committed to professional growth, regularly attending industry-led training to deepen his expertise and stay current in the automotive field.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

We’re excited to now share the Facebook post (link below) from Zion West Enterprises, celebrating the graduation of the first cohort in their solar program.

A big congratulations to Zion West Enterprises and to all of the solar program graduates! We’re incredibly proud of Zion’s quick and impactful work in launching this program, and we commend the graduates for their dedication and hard work.

RFP IS NOW CLOSED 4/21/25
REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP)

For Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Youth Services
in Boone, Stephenson, and Winnebago Counties
Program Year 2025 (07/01/2025-06/30/2026)

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ text_font_size=”17px” background_size=”initial” background_position=”top_left” background_repeat=”repeat” min_height=”475.9px” custom_padding=”||0px|||” global_colors_info=”{}”]

The Workforce Connection, Inc. (TWC) announces the release of Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) funding to an eligible organization or a consortium of eligible entities providing young adults ages 16 -24 (out of school) and 14-21 (in-school) workforce development services in Boone, Stephenson, and Winnebago Counties. The purpose of this RFP is to identify and fund an organization that will design and implement innovative programming and comprehensive training and education services that will result in youth participants achieving employment and academic success. Services should be delivered year-round to eligible Boone, Stephenson, and Winnebago Counties youth. WIOA youth programming is designed to assist in-school and out-of-school youth address one or more barriers to employment, preparing youth for post-secondary and employment opportunities, attain educational and/or skill credentials, and secure employment with promotional opportunities.

Many jobs requiring skilled training go unfilled because employers can’t find the talent they need. The overall goal of the youth program is to address the job-specific skills gaps of youth in Boone, Stephenson, and Winnebago Counties. The Workforce Connection is committed to implementing programs that produce a work-ready candidate for local employers.

To be considered for funding, providers must place an emphasis on work experience and credential/skill attainment that will improve the employment success of youth enrolled in the program. Providers must ensure that at least 25% of allocated funds be spent on work-based learning opportunities for youth. Work experience and skills training must focus on the demands of local employers, especially in high-growth industries and occupations identified in the regional workforce plan.

TWC is seeking an organization or consortium that provides employment and educational opportunities to young adults ages 16 -24 (out of school) and 14-21 (in-school) who are disconnected from school or work and can provide, both in-school and out-of-school youth, with easy access to a comprehensive and integrated set of training and education supports that increases the number of young adults that productively engage in the workforce.

Notice of Intent to Apply: By 5:00 m., April 10, 2025, potential bidders wishing to submit a proposal must submit a non-binding notification of intent to apply to TWC via email to BJaquez@TheWorkforceConnection.org. This notification must include the organization’s name and address, the contact staff member with title and e-mail address, and estimated funding request If applying as a consortium, all organizations must be identified, with the lead organization clearly identified.

Proposal Due Date: Proposals are due to TWC by noon on April 21, 2025 and can be emailed to BJaquez@TheWorkforceConnection.org or uploaded on The Workforce Connection’s website at www.TheWorkforceConnection.org  

www.TheWorkforceConnection.org/USDOLstatement

After working for an educational institution for 17 years, Deanna was laid off from her position. Although she held a bachelor’s degree, she lacked the specific skills needed to advance in her career. She had always been interested in office administration in a new field but was unsure of how to transition into a more professional, long-term, role.

Deanna came across the WIOA program through her local career center and decided to apply. Through the On the Job Training (OJT) program, Deanna secured an administrative assistant position at Doug Walker – Country Financial. The job involved managing client files, assisting with claims processing, obtaining insurance licensing, and supporting the company’s customer service operations. The WIOA program’s partnership with local businesses helped Deanna find a job where her newly gained skills were used immediately, and where her career prospects looked bright.

Within her first year, Deanna has proved to be an invaluable asset to the company. She has quickly adapted to the demands of the insurance industry and took on more responsibilities, including managing high-level correspondence and assisting with policy renewals. Deanna’s story is a testament to the power of training, support, and hard work. She is not only building a solid career but also helping her company grow and succeed in the competitive insurance industry.

The Workforce Connection, Inc. (TWC), the local workforce board is seeking proposals from organizations or a consortium of entities to provide One-Stop Operator Services and WIOA Title I Career Services for Adults, Dislocated Workers, and Trade. The service delivery area is Boone, Stephenson, and Winnebago Counties. The Workforce Connection, Inc. oversees three (3) service provision centers branded as The Workforce Connection, Inc. The comprehensive Center is located in Rockford, Illinois at 303 North Main Street. There are two (2) access sites – 524 W Stephenson Street, Suite 230, Freeport, Illinois, and 600 S State Street, 2nd Floor, Belvidere, Illinois.

The Workforce Connection, Inc. is committed to a public workforce development system that provides excellent customer service to both businesses and individuals. TWC is seeking a Service provider capable of delivering services utilizing a seamless system built on a “Service Integration” model. For the purposes of this scope of work, service integration is defined as a program delivery model that aligns, organizes and optimizes multiple actions with one common customer path. The service delivery model should have a clearly defined standardized process that generates measurable and successful outcomes for the wide range of services provided.

The provider(s) selected under this Request for Proposal will be expected to enhance our workforce development system by providing a fully coordinated and integrated customer service strategy, focused on a customer-centered model that offers value-added services to our career seekers and employer customers. Basic Career Services and specific program services, will be driven by four (4) key points –

    • Providing exceptional customer service;
    • Meeting the needs of business and workers;
    • Program integration to provide seamless access and increase service delivery; and
    • Accountability for performance and programmatic outcomes.

By close of business on Monday, March 24, 2025, potential bidders wishing to submit a proposal MUST submit a non-binding notification of intent to propose to The Workforce Connection, Inc. at BJaquez@TheWorkforceConnection.org. This notification must include the organization’s primary contact with title and e-mail address. All organizations must be identified if applying as a consortium, with a lead organization clearly identified.

Proposals are due to TWC by Noon Central Standard Time on Monday, April 7, 2025. Proposal should be emailed to BJaquez@TheWorkforceConnection.org 

www.TheWorkforceConnection.org/USDOLstatement 

 Posted February 27, 2025

The Workforce Connection’s Latrese Luton was honored by the Rockford Family Peace Center with their Partner of the Month Award.

 “At the FPC, we are fortunate to work with amazing partners from the community that are dedicated to advocating for survivors. Many of the survivors we serve experience barriers related to employment, and we rely on the collaboration we have built with local employment resources. We are very grateful to work with Latrese from the Workforce Connection, and we are pleased to share that she is our December Partner of the Month!

 Latrese is a Community Resource Navigator, and she is often our point of contact when referring survivors to TWC. Survivors can receive assistance with creating resumes, receiving job training, clothing needed for employment, childcare resources, and getting connected to local employers.

 Latrese’s kind, supportive, and compassionate nature shines through when working with our survivors. She truly makes a difference in the lives of our survivors and their children. Thank you, Latrese, for all you do!” (credit: Family Peace Center’s Facebook post).

 Latrese, pictured on the left, and an FPC staff member on the right, pose for a photo with the Partner of the Month award.

Jazmine Flores successfully completed her On-The-Job Training (OJT) at Midwest Law Works where her career path is to become a Real Estate Legal Assistant. Jazmine states she is very grateful to The Workforce Connection’s (TWC) Elevate Youth Program because she was able to gain valuable knowledge and obtain hands-on experience working directly for a real estate law firm. Jazmine states: “Without this opportunity, it would have been very difficult for me to get this direct training.” 

 Jazmine worked directly with Attorney Christian Solares and Paralegal Bethany Pederson who both commented on how she was able to quickly learn all the assignments they gave her and how her attention to detail was very precise. Jazmine was able to learn how to prepare affidavits, legal documents, correspondence and work directly with the clients.

Attorney Christian Solares stated: “There definitely is a future for Jazmine here at Midwest Law Works, and we are in the process of making that happen because she is very intelligent and bright, and we would love for her to become a permanent part of our team.”

“After earning my high school diploma through the GoodGrads Program, I took the necessary steps to achieve employment, with the help of The Workforce Connection a career center coordinator helped me with a professional resume. She crafted my resume and highlighted my skills, achievements, and aspirations.

I received constant encouragement from my mentors, who reminded me that my potential was limitless. Now having my high school diploma and a professional resume, I feel confident to dive in to the job market.

I look back on my journey with pride, knowing that each step–from my GED classes, to a high school diploma, to my job search, is a testament to my resilience and dedication to a better future.”

 Congratulations on your achievements Lonnie!

United Facilities Inc, a leader in distribution and logistics, faced a challenge in filling key warehousing roles. The company needed workers with specialized skills in Operations for their brand-new location in Belvidere, Illinois.

 Enter The Workforce Connection and its On-the-Job Training (OJT) program. United Facilities partnered with TWC, their local workforce development board, to craft a strategy that addressed their hiring and training needs.

 Through TWC, United Facilities was introduced to the OJT program, which offered a win-win solution:

 Cost-Effective Training: As a result of proper training and high employee retention, the OJT program allowed United Facilities to save money on training and onboarding costs.

  • Custom Training Plans: The program allowed United Facilities to design training tailored to their unique processes and equipment, ensuring new hires learned the exact skills needed.
  • Talent Matching: The local workforce board assisted United Facilities identifying candidates who were eager to learn but lacked the training and experience to work within United Facilities location.
  • Additional Support: The Workforce Connection posted open United Facilities positions on job seekers board and provided space to interview candidates at their facility. Additionally, they hosted job fairs that United Facilities could attend to find candidates that matched their hiring needs.

 The OJT Program provides results such as:

 Improved Workforce Quality: Over 80% of OJT participants successfully completed training and transitioned into long-term employment.

Community Impact: The partnership strengthened the local workforce by providing meaningful career pathways for individuals from underrepresented backgrounds.

Employer Testimonial:

 “Partnering with The Workforce Connection’s OJT program was a game-changer for United Facilities. It allowed us to grow our team with skilled, dedicated workers while minimizing turnover and training costs. The support we received from the workforce board was incredible, and we’ve gained employees who are not only trained but invested in our company’s success.” stated Courtney Chesser, Human Resources Generalist.

 This success story illustrates how the OJT program, supported by WIOA, can provide a practical and impactful solution for employers and job seekers alike.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

The Workforce Connection’s participant, Kierson, was featured in the Trade Adjustment Assistance (TAA) For Workers Program Annual Report.

 

“The TAA for Workers Program provides benefits and services to workers who are adversely affected by foreign trade. These benefits and service include employment and case management services, training, income support in the form of Trade Readjustment Allowances (TRA), job search allowances, and relocation allowances, and a wage insurance benefit for workers over 50 years of age called Reemployment TAA (RTAA) or Alternative TAA (ATAA).
In FY 2023, approximately 76.7% of TAA participants obtained new employment within 6 months of exiting the program. Median Earnings reached historic high levels in FY 2023 with reported earnings nearly 23% higher than FY 2019.
Wage replacement was also noteworthy for FY 2023, with post participation earnings at 106.5% of pre-participation employment earnings – the highest in known history of the TAA Program.” Source: Trade Adjustment Assistance (TAA) For Workers Program Annual Report-Page 2 and Success Story below-Page 4.

Kierson Eiland worked at Stellantis/FCA USA for almost 10 years and when the plant shut down, he attended a Rapid Response workshop and came to The Workforce Connection. He enrolled in the Trade program and was excited, yet a bit apprehensive about attending school again. He had been out of school for many years , but was looking forward to starting a new career for his family. As a single father of a daughter who has special needs, he knew it would not be easy, but he was ready and motivated.

 With assistance from his Career Planner, Kierson explored options and decided to become a welder. He enrolled in the Welding program at Rockford Career College, an 8-month, full-time program. After 8 challenging yet rewarding months, Kierson earned his Diploma in Welding! Very quickly after graduating, he obtained a position at Hennig Inc. as a Welder.

 Kierson is really enjoying his new career as a welder and enjoys using his new skills. His new career provides a livable wage and benefits, including health insurance , which is particularly important to him and his daughter. He stated “without the opportunity of this program, there was not an option for me to go to school. I would have had to just find another job, now I have something to build from.”

 When asked if he wanted to share anything else about his success and the WIOA and Trade programs, he said that he “highly recommends the program to anyone eligible and that they would be a fool not to take advantage of it”!

title.rendered: IWP Business Leadership Award Goes to Ultrasonic Power Corporation (UPC)

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.2″ _module_preset=”default” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″]

Ultrasonic Power Corporation (UPC), located in Freeport, Illinois, is on the cutting edge of the Industrial Ultrasonic Cleaner industry. Founded in 1972, UPC is a leading global ultrasonic cleaning company. They operate in an historic former railroad depot on eight acres and all products are “Made in the USA”, durable, industrial-grade precision cleaning equipment. UPC designs, develops, manufactures, distributes and supports our products from this single, technologically robust location.

 UPC is committed to exceptional precision industrial ultrasonic cleaning and liquid processing solutions, which extends not only to their customers, but to their commitment to workforce development and talent pipeline solutions. Over the past few years, UPC has worked with The Workforce Connection in various ways to not only connect with new candidates, but to provide training and upskilling for their current workforce.

Over the past 3 years, UPC has partnered with The Workforce Connection’s Business Services division in numerous ways. They have hired individuals from the WIOA Training and Employment Program, taking steps to ensure a robust training plan to ensure new staff have the skills they need to succeed on the job and advance in their careers. They have also utilized Incumbent Worker Training funds to provide continual training to current staff, ensuring that staff members and the organization can keep up with industry trends and continue to grow.

 LWIA 3 is so proud to work with UPC and recognize them for their continued efforts as a Business Leader in the region and the state.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

Arianna was in the process of getting her GED and was also looking for a work-based learning opportunity. Elevate was presenting at the Freeport Library and Arianna attended one of those presentations. While enrolled in Elevate, Arianna received assistance creating a resume, successfully completed a work-experience at Freeport Art Museum, and finished her GED within 3 months! She stated that her life is different now as she is better able to understand the responsibilities that come with having her first job. What she wants people to know about Elevate is that it was great that Elevate was able to find an appropriate work-experience that lines up with her career interests. She was able to learn Past Perfect, which is an archival database. Elevate made it easy to learn how to adult!

title.rendered: ICCTA Award to Bourn & Koch and Rock Valley College

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″ min_height=”1083.1px”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″]

Congratulations to Bourn & Koch and Rock Valley College, the 2024 Illinois Community College Trustees Association (ICCTA) award recipients in the Business/Industry Partnership Award category. This award recognizes Illinois businesses that have built successful workforce-training alliances with an ICCTA member college.

Our Board Vice-Chair, Todd Wells, who is Bourn & Koch’s Vice President of Operations was instrumental in this partnership along with Board member, Dr. Howard Spearman, and many others at Rock Valley College (RVC).

“With the investments made, and the mutual desire to grow the industry, we have seen many benefits at Bourn & Koch. With employees enrolling at RVC, and hiring recent graduates from RVC, we have seen this positively contribute to our onboarding experience in the machine shop along with increased productivity. We hope that our involvement at the RVC events will also lead to more manufacturing career interest and positively impact enrollment at RVC. Thank you to ICCTA for the recognition with the 2024 Business/Industry Partnership Award, and RVC for being a valued partner.” shared Bourn & Koch.

As quoted in a Rock Valley College website post (click here to view), “Bourn and Koch has been an essential partner in building the industry infrastructure for the next generation of manufacturing students. Bourn and Koch is one of the most active members of our manufacturing advisory committee, and their commitment to the college has provided careers for many of our students,” explained Dr. Hansen Stewart, RVC’s Vice President of Career Technical Education and Workforce Development.

Todd is thankful for all the support Bourn & Koch regularly receives from Dr. Spearman and the entire RVC team, teamwork that is essential to maintaining a talent pipeline.

Todd Wells is an RVC alumni. While at RVC, Todd obtained a mechanical design certificate, a master CAD certificate, and an Associate in Science in manufacturing engineering. He continued his studies at NIU to earn a Bachelor of Science in industrial engineering, a degree obtained primarily through attendance at RVC through the NIU/RVC partnership. Todd believes the investment at RVC was instrumental to creating the pathway to a prosperous career.

Way to go Bourn & Koch and Rock Valley College for paving the way in identifying needs in our local workforce and creating the pathways to fulfill them!

Click here to view Bourn & Koch’s full article.

Click here to visit the list of all the 2024 ICCTA Award Winners.
[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

More good news about the pharmacy technician internship program we told you about in the Innovative Partnerships section above…click the photo below to view the 23 WIFR video coverage.

A graduation ceremony was held on June 26th for the pharmacy technician internships at UW Health. We are so proud of all of our participants who were able to complete this program and thankful to Harlem High School and UW Health for partnering with us to provide this opportunity to their students.

We’d like to give a shout-out to TWC staff members Renee Austin, Karyn McDonald, Jessica Story, and the rest of the Youth team for working on this project and ensuring that 16 students began the program and all 16 completed successfully! Some of the students will continue on in an pharmacy technician apprenticeship program with UW Health.

Suzie recently graduated with honors from Rock Valley College’s Respiratory Care program (AAS). She quickly received a job offer and is set to begin at Rush University Medical Center as a license-pending Respiratory Therapist. Suzie utilized the WIOA program through The Workforce Connection which provided tuition assistance for her education.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.26.0″ _module_preset=”default” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″]

Adelbert recently completed a paid work experience with Winnebago County Housing Authority, where he helped run the cafeteria program and worked the food pantry monthly. After his work experience ended, he continued to volunteer because he enjoys the work. He has now secured employment with Goodwill Industries of Northern Illinois using his skills. When asked about his work experience with The Workforce Connection, he said, “it is a great program, it got me up and moving and helping others.” His advice was to stay with what you are doing and follow rules that are set up to help you learn. Congratulations Adelbert!

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.25.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.26.0″ _module_preset=”default” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″]

Jessica enrolled in the Elevate program in May of 2022. Jessica was a stay-at-home mother looking for employment and she expressed that she couldn’t seem to get a job, saying “I didn’t have my GED and had no experience.” So, she looked online for help finding agencies that could help people with little to no income. During her search, she found success stories from TWC’s ELEVATE program. While in the program, she successfully completed a GED program and went on to further her education beyond that.

 

Jessica would like others to know that “the program does not give up on you and they push you so you can achieve your goals”. Jessica appreciated the help with getting to her classes, exclaiming that “the bus passes and gas cards helped a lot.” She also noted that it was about more than finances though. It was about getting a person where they want to be in life.

 

Jessica is the proud recipient of a college diploma and is now a Registered Medical Assistant. Earning both her GED and a college degree, Jessica exclaims that she “feels more educated and respected”, also adding that her children “look at me as a leader!”.

With her recent passing of the RMA exam, Jessica’s next step is landing her dream job. 

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

June 5, 2024 – A press conference was held for the official signing of a new apprenticeship in Rockford, Illinois at Tad More Tailoring and Alterations. As a result of the extensive collaborative efforts between Tad More Tailoring and Alterations, The Workforce Connection, Inc., the United States Department of Labor, and local and State elected officials, we are pleased to announce that a new Industrial Sewing Apprenticeship has been approved by the US Department of Labor.
“This apprenticeship, the first of its kind in this field, will offer many individuals a life changing opportunity” said Dr. Gina Caronna, Executive Director, The Workforce Connection.
“I’m proud to support Tad More Tailoring in the creation of a new sewing apprenticeship program. Sewing is a critical skill that improves focus and concentration, as well as teaches the importance of patience and self-control. Participants will learn life-long skills and sustainable practices during this job training program.” said City of Rockford Mayor, Thomas McNamara.
“As the son of a master tailor and a small business owner, I spent more than 20 years working in the family tailoring business, learning not only skills of the trade, but also the importance of providing quality customer service,” said Winnebago County Board Chairman Joseph Chiarelli. “We are proud to support the Tad More Sustainability Institute Apprenticeship Program to encourage economic development in our community, promote job growth and pass on the art of tailoring.”
“By championing immigrant integration, fostering a positive work ethic, and prioritizing inclusivity, Tad More Tailoring embodies the essence of community empowerment and cultural enrichment. Our commitment to nurturing a diverse and talented workforce while upholding the principles of sustainable fashion underscores our unwavering dedication to making a meaningful difference in the world.” said Sarene Alsharif of Tad More Tailoring and Alterations
Thank you to everyone who attended to celebrate and to all of the speakers at the event. #workforcedevelopment #apprenticeship #jobs #rockford
[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

Our Mission: The Workforce Connection is committed to providing a workforce that meets the needs of the business community now and in the future.

Our Vision: Provide a fully integrated and accessible workforce development system that balances the needs of individuals and businesses to ensure our region has a skilled workforce to effectively compete in the global economy.

About the Board: The Workforce Connection (TWC) Board is one of 22 local workforce boards established by the Governor of the State of Illinois pursuant to the federal Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA). TWC’s Board of Directors and Chief Elected Officials are made up regional employers, educational institutions, economic development, public partners, and publicly elected officials, which guides the efforts of the organization and system.

Utilizing Federal, State, and donated funds, TWC provides a system for individuals to get employed and also works with employers to find skilled workers and access other services, including education and training for their current workforce in Boone, Stephenson, and Winnebago Counties. The partnerships with local agencies help foster the necessities in our tri-county area and ensure that both career seekers and employers are receiving the assistance they need to be successful. Our region’s workforce system is benefited by these partnerships to ensure that each person and business in our community knows to connect with the One-Stop Career Centers at the American Job Centers.

The Workforce Connection’s American Job Centers in Boone, Stephenson, and Winnebago counties are located at the addresses at the bottom of this website.   The main number is (815) 847-7574 and you can also get connected by emailing info@theworkforceconnection.org.

What is CEJA?

CEJA stands for the Climate and Equitable Jobs Act. CEJA Northern Illinois offers FREE training to prepare workers for a career in good-paying clean energy jobs. It includes hands on training, stipends for attending class, employment readiness skills, and job placement assistance. These programs are funded by the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO), and supports Illinois’s goal of phasing out carbon emissions from the energy and transportation sectors.

What is CEJA?

CEJA stands for the Climate and Equitable Jobs Act. CEJA Northern Illinois offers FREE training to prepare workers for a career in good-paying clean energy jobs. It includes hands on training, stipends for attending class, employment readiness skills, and job placement assistance. These programs are funded by the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO), and supports Illinois’s goal of phasing out carbon emissions from the energy and transportation sectors.

Is CEJA Right for Me?

CEJA meets you where you’re at, with few barriers to entry. Sign up if:

    • You’re looking for a new career in a growing field
    • You want a good-paying job with room to grow
    • You want to expand (or start) your business into clean energy
    • You need employment connections and career guidance
    • You have barriers that make traditional training or employment difficult

How does this initiative benefit our region?

    • Target participants are minorities and from underserved populations, providing these groups with a boost to change their futures.

    • The program is free – even paying participants stipends for achievements – and only lasts approximately 12 weeks, getting more people trained and into the workforce quickly.

    • By diversifying the workforce’s skillset and types of industries in the region, we are creating a more resilient economy to weather downturns.

    • Supports a wide variety of interests: entrepreneurs, renewable energy adoption, skilled trades, career changes.

The Workforce Connection– an Illinois workNet Center and partner in the American Job Center network. This program is subject to the provisions of the “Jobs for Veteran’s Act” Public Law 107-288, which provides priority of services to veterans and spouses of certain veterans. The Workforce Connection Job Board Terms and Conditions of Use

These Terms and Conditions of Use (the “Terms”) constitute a legal agreement between you (except as otherwise defined herein, a “User” or “Employer”) and The Workforce Connection (TWC) for the use of posting jobs on TWC’s Jobs Board on TWC’s website (www.TheWorkforceConnection.org). Access to and use of the Jobs Board by any User is subject to these Terms, including any modifications or additions to these Terms from time to time issued by TWC and all applicable laws and regulations. Accessing or using the Jobs Board indicates that User has reviewed these Terms, agrees to be bound by these Terms, and represents and warrants to TWC that User is authorized to enter into and be bound by these Terms on User’s behalf or on behalf of the entity that User represents.

TWC maintains the Jobs Board to facilitate employers posting open positions for job seekers to view and apply for the position through a link provided by the employer. Access to this Jobs Board is limited to that activity. Any access or attempt to access other areas of the TWC computer system or other information contained on the system for any purposes is strictly prohibited.

Rules

  1. The Jobs Board on TWC’s website is provided as a free service intended to connect job seekers with employers and job postings. All information posted must be related to the puposes of the Jobs Board.
  2. “Users” shall be defined as Employers or Job Seekers, as well as anyone else who uses TWC’s website. “Employers” shall be defined as all employees and agents of the employer who use the Jobs Board to post job openings. “Job Seekers” shall be defined as anyone who uses the Jobs Board who is not an Employer.
  3. Users who are Job Seekers (“Job Seekers”) are permitted to view job postings. Job seekers do not apply for jobs directly on the TWC Jobs Board, but may visit a link provided by the employer poster to apply for the job directly with the employer. No personal information is collected from Job Seekers visiting our Jobs Board.
  4. Job postings must be truthful and accurate, providing a realistic representation of the job, company, and opportunities.
  5. Employers should only post genuine job openings with a legitimate intent to hire for the specific position listed.
  6. Employers may not reference any third party organization to the job unless the application process is being handled by the named third party.
  7. Those using the Job Board for the purpose of posting employment opportunities shall abide by all local, state, and federal laws with regard to hiring and employment
  8. Postings should not intentionally misrepresent the job, hiring company, or poster.
  9. Any non-traditional working conditions or compensation (e.g., independent contractor, part-time, commission-based) must be clearly disclosed.
  10. Job postings cannot advertise for “business opportunities” that require payments or recruitment of others, or that resemble franchises, multi-level marketing, or club memberships.
  11. Employers cannot charge job seekers a fee to access job postings or apply for positions.
  12. Users are prohibited from uploading or distributing any information subject to trademark, copyright, or other proprietary rights except with the express consent of the owner of the rights.
  13. Users shall exercise both common sense and courtesy when posting information and shall not use the Jobs Board to transmit defamatory, disparaging, obscene or offensive materials or communications.
  14. The information and materials posted on TWC’s Jobs Board by Employer Users may contain errors, omissions, or typographical errors or may be out of date. The information and materials posted on this Jobs Board are provided for informational purposes only and are not binding on TWC in any way.
  15. Users shall respect the security of the Job Board and shall not attempt to delete or revise material posted by any other user or to gain access to areas private to TWC.
  16. The Jobs Board is not to be accessed to conduct any activities that may be illegal. For example, the Job Board shall not be used to encourage software infringement, spreading of computer viruses, or other crimes.
  17. Links and references to other Internet Websites operated by third parties do not constitute sponsorship, endorsement, or approval by TWC of the content, policies, or practices of such linked or referenced Websites. Linked and referenced Websites are not operated, controlled, or maintained by TWC, and TWC is not responsible for the availability, content, policies, or practices of linked or referenced Websites. Links and references to other Websites are provided for User’s convenience only, and User accesses them at User’s own risk.
  18. TWC reserves the right to to delete inactive Employer accounts on TWC’s Jobs Board.
  19. The Job Board is not to be used in a manner that violates the bylaws or any other policies, procedures, rules or regulations of TWC.

Limitation of Liability and Indemnity

TWC makes no warranty, guarantee, or representation as to the accuracy, sufficiency, or security of information posted by users and assumes no responsibility or liability in connection with the use or misuse of such information. TWC assumes no liability or responsibility for the quality, safety or legality of the employment opportunities or biographical information posted, the accuracy or truthfulness of the listings, or the ability of employers to offer employment opportunities to candidates. TWC reserves the right to monitor job postings and remove postings that it believes are not in the best interests of those using the Jobs Board or the best interests of TWC.

TWC’s Jobs Board is solely a platform and has no control over, and assumes no responsibility for, the content, privacy policies, or practices of any third-party companies, content, websites, or services. We do not warrant the offerings of any of these third-party entities/individuals or their websites.

TWC, its officers, directors, and employees, assume no liability or responsibility for any damages whatsoever (including, without limitation, incidental and consequential damages, lost profits, or damages resulting from lost data or business interruption) resulting from the use of, or inability to use, the Jobs Board, whether based on warranty, contract, tort, or any other legal theory, and whether or not the user is advised of the possibility of such damage.

Users who are Job Seekers accessing the Jobs Board shall indemnify and hold TWC harmless from and against any and all liability, claims, damages, losses, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) relating to any acts or omissions of the users or to materials or information transmitted by users in connection with their use of the job board.

It is against the law for The Workforce Connection to discriminate on the following bases:  against any individual in the United States, on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions, sex stereotyping, transgender status, and gender identity), national origin (including limited English proficiency), age, disability, or political affiliation or belief, or, against any beneficiary of, applicant to, or participant in programs financially assisted under Title I of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, on the basis of the individual’s citizenship status or participation in any WIOA Title I–financially assisted program or activity.

The Workforce Connection must not discriminate in any of the following areas: deciding who will be admitted, or have access, to any WIOA Title I-financially assisted program or activity; providing opportunities in, or treating any person with regard to, such a program or activity; or making employment decisions in the administration of, or in connection with, such a program or activity.

Recipients of federal financial assistance, such as The Workforce Connection, must take reasonable steps to ensure that communications with individuals with disabilities are as effective as communications with others. This means that, upon request and at no cost to the individual, recipients are required to provide appropriate auxiliary aids and services to qualified individuals with disabilities.

Auxiliary aids and services are available upon request to individuals with disabilities. All voice telephone numbers on our website theworkforceconnection.org may be reached by persons using TTY/TDD equipment by calling TTY (800) 526-0844 or 711.

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.6″ _module_preset=”default” custom_padding=”||0px|||” global_colors_info=”{}”]

WHAT TO DO IF YOU BELIEVE YOU HAVE EXPERIENCED DISCRIMINATION

If you think that you have been subjected to discrimination under a WIOA Title I–financially assisted program or activity, you may file a complaint within 180 days from the date of the alleged violation. You can file in one of the following ways:

Equal Opportunity Officer, Emily Welsh
The Workforce Connection
303 N. Main Street, Rockford IL 61101
(779)256-2008 TDD/TTY 800-526-0844
ewelsh@theworkforceconnection.org
or
Equal Opportunity Officer
Illinois Department of Commerce & Economic Opportunity
1011 S. 2nd Street, Springfield, IL 62704
(217)588-2418
or
Director, Civil Rights Center (CRC), U.S. Department of Labor
200 Constitution Avenue NW, Room N-4123, Washington, DC 20210
or electronically as directed on the CRC website at www.dol.gov/crc

If you file your complaint with The Workforce Connection, you must wait either until the recipient issues a written Notice of Final Action, or until 90 days have passed (whichever is sooner), before filing with the Civil Rights Center (see address above). If the recipient does not give you a written Notice of Final Action within 90 days of the day on which you filed your complaint, you may file a complaint with CRC before receiving that Notice. However, you must file your CRC complaint within 30 days of the 90-day deadline (in other words, within 120 days after the day on which you filed your complaint with the recipient).

If The Workforce Connection does give you a written Notice of Final Action on your complaint, but you are dissatisfied with the decision or resolution, you may file a complaint with CRC. You must file your CRC complaint within 30 days of the date on which you received the Notice of Final Action.

What is a Workforce Board?

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.17.4″ header_3_font=”|300|||||||” header_3_text_color=”#0c71c3″ header_3_font_size=”33px” min_height=”313.2px” custom_padding=”||0px|||” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Workforce Development Boards (WDBs) have a critical role to play in contributing to healthy regional economies that serve the needs of business and workers.

WDBs function in multiple roles—as a steward of Federal and non-Federal funds, overseeing a host of operational systems and processes, and as the primary architects of the State’s overall workforce strategy. 

Our Board of Directors and Chief Elected Officials work in collaboration with The Workforce Connection staff to strategically address the following priorities:

        • Integrate workforce, education, and economic development efforts to move the Region forward.
        • Engage employers as champions for workforce solutions that meet their current and future needs.
        • Increase skill level of the workforce through bolstered education and training opportunities.
        • Connect residents of all skill levels and socioeconomic groups to career opportunities.
        • Improve intake, tracking, and data management systems.
        • Promote the benefits of the workforce system to residents and employers.
[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ header_3_font=”|300|||||||” header_3_text_color=”#0c71c3″ header_3_font_size=”33px” min_height=”40px” custom_margin=”||32px|||” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″]

What does it mean to be a Board Member?

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.17.4″ header_3_font=”|300|||||||” header_3_text_color=”#0c71c3″ header_3_font_size=”33px” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Do you want to play a part in the economic vitality of Northern Illinois?

Our incredible Board of Directors and Chief Elected Officials are involved in the success of Boone, Stephenson, and Winnebago counties in their daily professional life.

Being on The Workforce Connection’s Board means being connected to other Executives in the region and local and State politicians, guiding the agile public workforce development system, and solving specific workforce challenges affecting businesses and individuals.

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ header_3_font=”|300|||||||” header_3_text_color=”#0c71c3″ header_3_font_size=”33px” custom_margin=”||32px|||” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″]

How do I know if I’m eligible?

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ header_3_font=”|300|||||||” header_3_text_color=”#0c71c3″ header_3_font_size=”33px” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″]

Board Members for The Workforce Connection must:

  • Desire to make a positive contribution to the local area or region’s economy, by helping to shape a workforce development system that meets the needs of employers and career-seekers;
  • Have optimum decision-making authority for their organzation which does business in or resides within Boone, Stephenson, or Winnebago Counties of Illinois;
  • Commit to devoting 4-6 hours per quarter and expertise working with other Board members, staff, businesses, public officials, and public and private sector partnerships to improve the quality of the workforce, and;
  • Work for an organization that falls into our targeted industries. As this changes with the nature of workforce, we ask you indicate your primary industry in your application.

Statement of Accessibility

Meeting locations are accessible to individuals with physical disabilities, in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Auxiliary aids are available up request.
